column1: In the pinhole camera model, what are the perspective projection equations mapping a 3D camera-frame point [X, Y, Z] to pixel coordinates [u, v]?
column2: u = f · X / Z and v = f · Y / Z, where f is the focal length. The division by Z introduces the depth ambiguity that makes monocular depth estimation inherently underconstrained.

column1: Why does a point [X, Y, Z] and a point [2X, 2Y, 2Z] project to the identical pixel location in a monocular camera?
column2: Because perspective projection divides by depth Z, scaling both numerator and denominator equally cancels out, producing the same [u, v]—this is the fundamental scale/depth ambiguity of monocular vision.

column1: Write the full projection equation from homogeneous world coordinates to pixel coordinates, and identify each matrix component.
column2: λ[u, v, 1]^T = K[R | t]P, where K is the 3×3 intrinsic matrix (focal lengths, principal point), R and t are the camera's rotation and translation relative to the world frame, P is the homogeneous world point, and λ is an arbitrary scale factor.

column1: What two components make up the intrinsic matrix K, and why might f_x and f_y differ?
column2: K encodes focal lengths (f_x, f_y) and the principal point (c_x, c_y) where the optical axis meets the image plane. f_x and f_y can differ due to non-square (rectangular) pixel geometry on the sensor.

column1: Distinguish radial distortion from tangential distortion in a camera lens.
column2: Radial distortion is a nonlinear warping displacing points radially inward (pincushion) or outward (barrel) from the image center. Tangential distortion arises from imperfect lens-sensor alignment, causing asymmetric displacement.

column1: What is the epipolar geometry constraint, and why is it computationally critical for stereo depth recovery?
column2: Given two camera views of the same scene, corresponding points must lie on conjugate epipolar lines. This reduces correspondence search from a 2D image-wide search to an efficient 1D search along the epipolar line.

column1: What is the key distinction between passive computer vision and spatial computing in robotic perception?
column2: Passive computer vision classifies/detects objects in 2D imagery, while spatial computing builds a geometrically faithful, semantically enriched 3D model that a robot can navigate, reason about, and interact with in real time.

column1: Name the three major sensor modalities used in robotic AR sensor fusion and their core complementary limitation.
column2: IMU (high-frequency, zero latency, but drifts unboundedly via integration), Visual Odometry (drift-free absolute position, but lower update rate due to exposure/feature-matching latency), and LiDAR (millimeter precision, lighting-invariant, but limited by scan rate/FOV/resolution trade-offs).

column1: What invariant property of the Bayesian sensor fusion update rule justifies combining IMU, camera, and LiDAR data in any order or combination?
column2: The Bayesian update is both commutative and associative across sensor modalities—fusing sensors in any order or all at once yields identical optimal posterior estimates, given correctly modeled noise characteristics.

column1: In human-robot AR interaction, what is the 'attentional bandwidth' invariant, and why does it constrain overlay design?
column2: Although the visual cortex processes ~30 million bits/second, conscious awareness handles only 40-50 bits/second. Every AR overlay element competes for this scarce bandwidth; overloading it causes operator errors and reversion to manual control.

column1: What is 'trust calibration' in robotic AR interfaces, and what happens when it fails in each direction?
column2: Trust calibration means visualizing not just robot actions but their confidence/safety margins (e.g., grasp success probability, collision risk). Poor calibration causes either over-reliance (ignoring warnings) or under-reliance (micro-managing every motion), both degrading performance and safety.

column1: In the robotic AR verification lab setup, what reprojection error threshold must Zhang's camera calibration method achieve, and what distortion model parameters are extracted?
column2: Reprojection error below 0.3 pixels RMS must be achieved, extracting a 3×3 camera intrinsic matrix K and a five-parameter radial-tangential distortion vector.
